weaknesses: The main theoretical claims exceed the results proved. Consequently, the reported gains cannot be confidently attributed to cautious masking.

Results appear to be single runs without seeds, error bars, or significance tests. The claimed 1.47x speedup is not precisely defined, and no wall-clock or throughput measurements support the claim of virtually no overhead despite the added masking and reduction operations.

Several evaluations are too weak to substantiate task-agnostic or universal improvement. Reproducibility and positioning are incomplete: schedules, warmup, model configurations, data processing, evaluation details, seeds, and most post-training settings are missing; the promised code link is absent; and comparisons omit both recent optimizers discussed in related work and closely relevant sign-alignment or update-masking approaches. The strongest scaling gains are only 0.10–1.00%, with no independent training seeds or uncertainty estimates. Every reported downstream difference is smaller than the displayed evaluation uncertainty, so describing C-AdamW as winning five of seven tasks is not persuasive statistical evidence.
